# LeakSanitizer suppressions for the loft interpreter ASan leak gate (@PLN85).
# Syntax: `leak:<substr>` suppresses any leak whose stack contains a frame whose
# demangled name contains <substr>.
#
# The interpreter interns IR node/schema/store names (and reconstructed string
# content) as `&'static str` via an intentional, bounded `Box::leak` (interner-style,
# not a growing leak) when loading IR back from a store. The SAME class lives in three
# sibling modules — the demangled allocating frame names the module, so each needs its
# own line: `loft::ir_read::{read_db_content,read_block,read_definition}`,
# `loft::ir_schema::{block_from_parsed,definition_from_parsed}`, and
# `loft::database::snapshot::content_from`. ~16 ir_read/ir_schema/store round-trip lib
# tests report it. Documented in miri.yml. These are the ONLY classes suppressed; every
# real interpreter leak stays visible and is gated by the shrinking count baseline
# (scripts/asan_leak_ratchet.sh). NOTE: matching requires SYMBOLIZED stacks — the leak
# gate sets ASAN_SYMBOLIZER_PATH so these frame names resolve.
leak:ir_read
leak:ir_schema
leak:database::snapshot

# The fault-path text class (@PLN102).  When a loft program raises a fault (a failed
# `assert`, `panic`, a `raise`d OOB/DivByZero) WHILE a text is mid-construction, the
# compiler-emitted drop of that in-flight text local never runs, so its `String` buffer
# is live at exit.  This is an ACCEPTED non-cleanup on the terminating abort path, NOT a
# production leak: the real binary `process::exit`s on a fault, so LSan never runs there;
# it only surfaces in-process (the dozens of `should_panic` / `.error()` fixtures and the
# `raise(...)` scripts).  Freeing in-flight text on the abort path would need the
# coroutine-style zeroing/double-drop discipline on the hot call path — a risky change out
# of proportion to a non-production leak.  Non-faulting execution frees text normally, so
# these frames only ever fire on the fault path.  The four text-construction entry points:
leak:fill::append_text
leak:ops::format_text
leak:ops::format_long
leak:text_tl_fmt

# macOS dyld thread-local storage term-func registration on a spawned thread
# (the test harness watchdog): `dyld::ThreadLocalVariables::addTermFunc`, reached
# via `thread_start`. A one-per-thread SYSTEM allocation, not a loft heap leak — and
# absent on the Linux CI leg (different TLS impl), so this line is a macOS-only no-op
# there. Specific to the dyld frame so it never masks a real loft leak.
leak:addTermFunc
